extracted.intended_audience: chemical indexers, patent searchers/examiners, cheminformatics/data curators who assign chemical structure codes to patent documents
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and coding rules for assigning hierarchical chemical indexing codes (ring systems and functional groups) to organic compounds in patent documents. Covers how to select codes, handling of heteroatoms, substituent positional conventions, tautomerism, spiro/poly annotations, and the use of negation/essential codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchy and digit-meanings for Part F codes
rubrics_metrics.description: The codes in Part F: are hierarchical. In all Sets except F0:, the first digit indicates the heteroatom(s) present; the second digit identifies the specific type of ring system present; and the third digit indicates the state of hydrogenation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In most codes a final “0” means that the code covers all hydrogenation states; “1” means fully unsaturated; “2” means intermediate saturation; and “3” means fully saturated. Each code also covers rings in which 1 or more C atoms have been replaced by heteroatoms other than O, S, N, Se, or Te, and rings in which one or more S atoms have been replaced by Se or Te.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ring-position vs. total-number rule for Part F substituents
rubrics_metrics.description: The ring positions of atoms bearing substituents are searched (not the total number of ring atoms bearing substituents as in Parts D: and G:).

rubrics_metrics.name: Heterocyclic ring numbering (IUPAC priority) in Part F
rubrics_metrics.description: The numbering of heterocyclic rings follows IUPAC conventions. Numbering starts with the highest priority heteroatom, and then the rest of the ring is numbered in the direction yielding the lowest possible number(s) for the remaining heteroatom(s).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The heteroatom priority is: O > S > N (descending group order).

rubrics_metrics.name: F017 / F018 substitution codings
rubrics_metrics.description: F017 indicates that two substituents are on the same C atom in the ring. F018 indicates that two or more substituents are on the same heteroatom.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of Poly in Part F
rubrics_metrics.description: Poly is used when different rings have the same positions substituted, not when there are multiple substituents on the same ring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spiro handling in Part F
rubrics_metrics.description: Spiro rings are considered one substituent; a ring spiro to a mononuclear heterocycle receives the spiro code F022.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability dates / subheadings for Part F codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes F000 to F019 are applicable to subheadings M1 to M4 from 1981 forward. All other codes apply to M0 from 1963 and to M1, M2, M3 and M4 from 1970 forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hierarchy and digit-meanings for Part G codes
rubrics_metrics.description: The codes in Part G: are hierarchical. In most cases the first digit indicates whether the ring is aromatic or alicyclic and the number of rings; the second digit indicates the type of ring system present; and the third digit indicates the state of hydrogenation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A final “0” means the code covers all hydrogenation states; “1” fully unsaturated; “2” intermediate saturation; “3” fully saturated. Each code also covers rings in which one or more C atoms have been replaced by heteroatoms other than O, S, N, Se, or Te.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'aromatic' for Part G (rings coded as aromatic)
rubrics_metrics.description: Ring systems are considered aromatic if they consist only of C atoms and if one or more of certain reference rings (essentially benzene-like / quinonoid derivatives) is present in fused or unfused state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The manual treats 'aromatic' nearly synonymously with fused or unfused benzene and includes the fused or unfused quinonoid derivatives of benzene. Aromatic rings are searched using codes in Sets G1: through G4:.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hydrogenated derivatives inclusion for aromatic codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Unless specifically excluded, codes also cover hydrogenated derivatives, provided that at least one ring in the system is aromatic.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: G310 includes fluorene plus its 1,2-dihydro- and 1,2,3,4-tetrahydro- derivatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alicyclic ring system coding (Part G)
rubrics_metrics.description: All carbocyclic ring systems that are not aromatic are searched using a code from Set G5: to G8:.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consider each ring individually in fused carbocycles
rubrics_metrics.description: Each ring in a fused carbocyclic system is considered individually when selecting codes for substituents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Meaning of substituent-number in G01-G03
rubrics_metrics.description: The substituent number in codes from Subsets G01: to G03: refers to the number of C atoms in each ring that bear substituents. The second set of numbers (in parentheses on the coding sheet) refers to the relative positions in the ring of the C atoms bearing substituents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alpha / beta specification for fused aromatic substituent (G020/G021)
rubrics_metrics.description: If only one atom of a fused benzene ring bears substituent(s), the position of the substituent(s) can be specified as adjacent (alpha) or not adjacent (beta) to ring fusion using codes G020 and G021, respectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relative-position specification for multiple substituents in unfused aromatic rings
rubrics_metrics.description: If two or three C atoms in an unfused aromatic ring bear substituents, the relative positions of the substituents can be specified (e.g. G015 indicates positions 1,2,4).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The numbers refer to relative positions in the ring, not conventional numbering. Quinonoid substituents are counted and coded like any other aromatic substituents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Single-substituent codes for alicyclic rings (G030-G032)
rubrics_metrics.description: If only one atom in an unfused alicyclic ring bears substituents, use G030. If one atom of a fused alicyclic ring bears substituents, its position can be specified as adjacent (alpha) or not adjacent (beta) to ring fusion using G031 and G032.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple-substituent relative-positioning in alicyclic rings (G034 etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: If there are two atoms in a fused or unfused alicyclic ring that bear substituents, the relative positions can be specified (e.g. G034 = substituents on two adjacent alicyclic C atoms). Lowest possible numbers are always assigned to the substituents.

rubrics_metrics.name: Spiro handling for carbocycles (G041/G052)
rubrics_metrics.description: Spiro groups are considered one substituent. A ring spiro to a carbocycle is additionally assigned one of the carbocyclic spiro codes G041 (aromatic) or G052 (alicyclic), depending on the type of carbocycle to which the ring is spiro.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Note: G041 is assigned when a ring is spiro to an alicyclic ring that is fused to benzene; G052 is not assigned in such cases, except if the first ring is alicyclic, when both codes would be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability dates / subheadings for Part G codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Subsets G00:, G01:, G02:, G03:, G06:, and G11: are applicable to subheadings M1 to M4 from 1981 forward. All other codes apply to M0 from 1963 and to M1, M2, M3 and M4 from 1970 forward.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle: use the least number of functional group codes
rubrics_metrics.description: Coders should use the least possible number of functional group codes to describe functional groups; many codes may appear applicable but rules restrict which are actually used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reduces redundancy; detailed rules for choosing applicable codes are provided in the 'Choosing Applicable Functional Group Codes' section.

rubrics_metrics.name: One-character symbol definitions for functional-group code templates
rubrics_metrics.description: One-character symbols are used as shorthand in code definitions (T, U, V, W, X, Y, Z) to represent groups of elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definitions: T = O, S, Se, Te; U = O, S, Se, Te or N; V = heteroatom other than O,S,Se,Te or N; W = O,S,Se,Te,N,C or halogen in Parts H: through L:; X = any heteroatom in Parts other than H: through L:; Y = halogen (F, Cl, Br, I); Z = O,S,Se,Te,N or halogen; and B, Si, P or As are used where indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional-group-in-ring rule and exceptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional group codes from Parts H:, J:, K:, and L: are usually not assigned to groups having more than one atom in the same ring system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions include L710, certain designated codes in Set H7:, Set K1:, Set L8:, and Set L9:; see code definitions (examples provided).

rubrics_metrics.name: Se/Te substitution rule for functional groups
rubrics_metrics.description: A compound with an Se or Te atom receives all codes from Parts H: through L: that would be applicable if Se or Te were replaced by S. In addition, the Se and Te atoms are themselves assigned codes from Part B:.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: H494 ('-SH group bonded to an aromatic ring') is assigned to structures even when Se is present; the structure with Se also gets a Part B code for selenium.

rubrics_metrics.name: Functional groups bonded to metals: two-case rule
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional groups in organic ions or ligands that are bonded to a metal atom via C are searched in Parts H: through L: in one of two ways: (a) as if the metal were replaced by H when the metal is bonded to only one C atom, or (b) as if the metal were replaced by C when the metal is bonded to more than one C atom.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: Mg salt of HOCH2CH2NH2 is searched as H181 and H481 (as if metal replaced by H). More complete guidelines appear in Part A.

rubrics_metrics.name: Codes for groups bonded to B, Si, P, As (Z atoms)
rubrics_metrics.description: Functional groups bonded to B, Si, P, and As (i.e. 'Z' atoms) are coded in Subset B79:. Some of these functional groups are additionally coded in Parts H: through L:.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guidelines for searching for functional groups bonded to Z atoms are found elsewhere in the manual (page 48).

rubrics_metrics.name: Choosing applicable functional-group codes: search order
rubrics_metrics.description: If a functional group contains a bond between heteroatoms, first look for matching codes in Part K:. If no bonds between heteroatoms are present, begin looking for applicable codes in Part L:.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the atoms and bonds are not completely described by the first matching code, then look for further matching codes in the order that the Sets appear (first K:, then L:). By convention choose the minimum number of codes that together identify every atom of the group and all bonds; at each stage choose the largest possible matching group even if this means an atom is covered by multiple codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not add less-specific codes that add no information
rubrics_metrics.description: Codes occurring later in a Part or Set are often less specific or cover fewer atoms than the first applicable code(s); such less-specific codes are not used if they add no new information about the structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: a structure coded L511 would not also be coded as L512; K340 would not be followed by K352 if it adds nothing new.

rubrics_metrics.name: When to add codes that identify template symbols
rubrics_metrics.description: If the definition of an applicable code includes variable element symbols (T, U, V, W, X, Y and/or Z), additional codes are used to identify the elements represented by the symbols, unless the first code states this should not be done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: code L410 may require adding K820 and L463 to identify T, U and Y. Note exceptions (e.g. note 5 on page 162 says no additional codes should identify 'T' for L620).

rubrics_metrics.name: Fallback to Parts H and J when K/L insufficient
rubrics_metrics.description: If all functional groups in a structure have not been fully defined by codes from Parts K: and L:, Parts H: and J: can be scanned for relevant codes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although groups like amine, hydroxy, ester, amide etc. are easily identifiable, they are often coded in Part K: or Part L: because of the atoms to which they are bonded. Examples show when L-codes are used instead of similar H/J codes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tautomerism rule 1: keto-enol (thioxo-thiol) handling
rubrics_metrics.description: When keto-enol (thioxo-thiol) tautomerism is possible, the structure is searched in the keto (thioxo) form, unless the -OH (-SH) group of the enol (thiol) form is bonded to a fully conjugated carbocyclic ring.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: If -OH is bonded to a fully conjugated ring (e.g. benzene-like), code the enol form (-OH) instead of keto. Several illustrative examples (a–f) show when to prefer H (enol/phenolic) codes vs J (oxo) codes and how ring conjugation affects choice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tautomerism rule 2: imine tautomerization in rings
rubrics_metrics.description: An imine group (>C=N-) in which the C atom is part of a ring is tautomerized and searched in the =C-NH- form if such tautomerization causes the N atom to form an amine or amide group. If the tautomerization leads to an N group other than amine or amide, the imine form is coded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: K630 ('N-N=C') is used not K640 or K534; a ring imine may be searched as H121 ('1 amine bonded to a heterocycle') rather than L355 ('C=N') if tautomerization produces an amine.

rubrics_metrics.name: Negation (essential) codes usage
rubrics_metrics.description: The two-character codes at the beginning of each Set in Parts H:, J:, K:, and L: are negation codes (essential codes). Negation codes are searched negatively by users to eliminate false drops retrieved by chemical code searches.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Four-character chemical codes are searched with the LINK operator; negation codes are negated using LINK NOT.
